title: Mi Lexio
summary: A Spanish-language PWA for the Catholic daily readings: the readings and gospel for the day, a short reflection, offline reading and home-screen install, backed by its own API.
role: Solo — the client, its reading experience and the API platform behind it.
context: The daily readings are published every day, and reading them on a phone usually means a page full of navigation, ads and layout shifts. The point of this project was a single calm screen: today's readings, the sections that belong to the day, and nothing else.

solution.title: Today, not a library
solution.body: One screen with tabbed sections for the first reading, psalm, second reading and gospel, plus date navigation for the days around it. The reading itself is the liturgical text; generated enrichment is labelled as generated.

solution.title: Reads offline once opened
solution.body: A service worker caches the shell and the last reading, and the app installs to the home screen. Text-to-speech and the share sheet use the browser APIs, so listening and sharing cost no extra service.

contribution: Solo project. I built the client and the API behind it: the reading model, the date handling, the offline shell and the enrichment fields the screen renders.
approach: The client has no build step on purpose. It is a small static app that speaks to one API, which keeps the deploy cheap and the failure modes visible. The interesting constraint is the calendar: readings follow a liturgical day, not the user's device timezone, so the API decides what “today” means and the client only navigates around it.
confidentialityNote: Generated reflections are labelled in the product; the liturgical readings are not model output.
evidenceNote: Verified against the public dreading-pwa and dreading-api repositories and the live deployment on 2026-11-25. The owner brief names the product Mi Lexio; the public deployment is branded “Lectura del día” and the code lives in the dreading repositories. Milexio had no resolvable deployment at verification time, so no such URL is published.
